analyst.summary: Safari continues to grow revenue at a healthy mid-to-high-teens pace by taking share in the value/economy luggage segment, but that share gain has come at the cost of margin compression (operating margins down from ~18% to ~13% over two years), so profit growth is running behind revenue growth. The balance sheet is healthy and debt is being paid down, but at roughly 47x earnings the stock already prices in continued strong execution -- there is limited room for a slip in margins or growth without a valuation reset.
